"PROJECT: VOXEL ADVENTURES — MOBILE OPEN-WORLD RPG

1. MAIN OBJECTIVE

Develop a 3D open-world action-adventure RPG primarily inspired by the gameplay experience of Cube World Alpha (2013).

The game should preserve the essence of the original Alpha version: free exploration, traditional experience-based progression, character development, procedural world generation, different biomes, creatures, companions, quests, equipment, and skill systems.

The project must be a complete, functional, and playable game optimized for Android and iOS devices.

Create an original game with its own visual identity, characters, names, models, and assets. Do not directly copy copyrighted assets or proprietary content from Cube World.

2. VISUAL STYLE

- 3D voxel-based world with a blocky aesthetic.
- Characters, trees, buildings, mountains, and creatures constructed from voxel-inspired geometry.
- Vibrant colors and fantasy environments.
- Dynamic lighting and shadows.
- Day and night cycle.
- Dynamic weather, including rain, snow, and fog.
- Smooth character and creature animations.
- Third-person camera perspective.

The visual style should recreate the feeling of adventure and discovery found in classic voxel RPGs.

3. CHARACTER CREATION

Allow players to create and customize their own characters.

Include:

- Different races and appearances.
- Hair, face, and color customization.
- Four main classes: Warrior, Ranger, Mage, and Rogue.
- Visible equipment on character models.
- Ability to create and save multiple characters.

Each class must have unique abilities, attributes, and gameplay styles.

4. CHARACTER PROGRESSION SYSTEM

Implement a traditional RPG progression system:

- Enemies grant experience points.
- Characters gain levels.
- Each level grants skill points.
- Attributes improve as characters progress.
- New abilities are gradually unlocked.
- Equipment comes in different rarities and provides different attributes.
- Characters retain their progression when exploring different regions.

Do not use the region-based progression system introduced in the 2019 version of Cube World.

5. SKILL SYSTEM

Create individual skill trees for each character class.

Include active, passive, and special abilities.

Also implement general adventure abilities:

- Climbing.
- Swimming.
- Sailing.
- Gliding.
- Taming.
- Mount riding.

Skills should improve through points earned by the player.

6. PROCEDURAL OPEN WORLD

Create a large, procedurally generated world with different terrain types and structures.

Include biomes such as:

- Forests.
- Deserts.
- Mountains.
- Grasslands.
- Snow-covered regions.
- Swamps.
- Volcanic areas.
- Magical regions.

The world should contain:

- Villages.
- Cities.
- Caves.
- Dungeons.
- Castles.
- Ancient ruins.
- Lakes and rivers.
- Oceans.
- Towers and abandoned structures.

Each world must have a World Seed system, allowing players to generate the same world again using the same seed.

Exploration should be completely free, without forcing players to follow a linear campaign.

7. CREATURES AND COMPANIONS

Create a wide variety of creatures with unique behaviors.

Implement a taming system:

- Discover creatures throughout the world.
- Find out which foods they prefer.
- Earn their trust.
- Recruit companions that follow the player.
- Companions can assist during battles and adventures.
- Some creatures can be used as mounts.
- Companions have their own attributes and progression systems.

8. COMBAT SYSTEM

Develop real-time combat featuring:

- Basic attacks.
- Special abilities.
- Dodging.
- Blocking.
- Combos.
- Enemies with different combat behaviors.
- Bosses with unique attack patterns.

Each character class must provide a distinct combat experience.

9. EQUIPMENT AND CRAFTING

Implement a complete inventory system containing:

- Weapons.
- Armor.
- Accessories.
- Potions.
- Materials.
- Food.
- Special items.

Add a crafting system that allows players to create equipment using materials collected during ex (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable original mobile 3D voxel open-world RPG inspired by classic exploration-focused RPG gameplay.

## Requirements
- Original visual identity and assets; do not copy Cube World content.
- Mobile Android/iOS support, responsive touch controls, third-person 3D voxel world.
- Include character classes/customization, persistent traditional XP progression, skills, seeded procedural biomes/world, creatures/taming/companions, real-time combat, quests, inventory, and crafting.
- Do not use region-based progression.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a browser-based Three.js game in a single `index.html`, with original name “Wildbound.”
- Used procedural geometry and terrain, an eight-biome palette, a fixed camera-follow view, and mobile virtual controls.
- Chose a compact playable slice: four classes and three ancestries, one hamlet, local rumor quest, three creature types, a tameable fox companion, combat/progression, inventory, and crafting.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with the game’s setup screen, HUD, Three.js world, procedural terrain/decor, hamlet, enemies, combat, XP leveling, companion taming, crafting/inventory/skills/journal panels, minimap, day/night cycle, keyboard and touch controls.
- Started a local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Installed Playwright Chromium and opened the page at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Started a game session in browser and saved a JPEG screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/wildbound.jpg`.

### Active
- Validate gameplay and fix any discovered issues; the screenshot was opened but not described or used for further adjustments.

### Blocked
- No known blockers.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/wildbound.jpg` if visual validation is still needed; capture a fresh screenshot after any changes.
2. Test game start, movement, combat, leveling, companion, crafting, and mobile layout in Playwright.
3. Check `git status` and summarize the implementation and any limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation.

## Important Context
- Playwright showed no game runtime errors after starting; only a missing `/favicon.ico` 404 and WebGL readback performance warnings.
- Changes are uncommitted; no package manifest or build system was present.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable original mobile 3D voxel open-world RPG inspired by classic exploration-focused RPG gameplay.

## Requirements
- Original visual identity and assets; do not copy Cube World content.
- Support Android/iOS with responsive touch controls, third-person 3D voxel world, and free exploration.
- Include character classes/customization, persistent XP progression, skills, seeded procedural biomes/world, creatures and companions, real-time combat, quests, inventory, and crafting.
- Do not use region-based progression.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a browser-based Three.js game in a single `index.html`, titled “Wildbound.”
- Chose a compact playable slice: four classes, three ancestries, a hamlet, a local rumor quest, three creature types, a tameable fox companion, combat/progression, crafting/inventory/skills/journal panels, minimap, and day/night cycle.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the Wildbound game interface, procedural voxel-inspired world, character setup, HUD, combat, progression, companion, crafting, and mobile controls in `index.html`.
- Started a local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Opened `http://localhost:3002` in Playwright, started a game session, and saved `/tmp/opencode/wildbound.jpg`.
- Confirmed the game starts without runtime errors; browser reported a missing `/favicon.ico` and WebGL readback performance warnings.
- Added a `terrainHeight(x,z)` helper to `index.html` after reviewing the terrain implementation.

### Active
- Validate gameplay and mobile layout; inspect the latest screenshot and fix any discovered issues.
- Check whether `terrainHeight` should be applied to entities and structures so they align with the procedurally varied ground.

- (none)

1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/wildbound.jpg` and capture a fresh screenshot after any changes.
2. Test movement, combat, leveling, companion taming, crafting, and mobile layout in Playwright.
3. Review terrain/entity alignment and use `terrainHeight` if needed.
4. Check `git status` and summarize the implementation and limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.
